title: New glass igloos and hotels in Lapland for winter 2026–27
seoTitle: New glass igloos and hotels in Lapland, winter 2026–27
description: Two new glass igloo resorts are already taking guests in Rovaniemi. More places to stay open this winter in Muonio, Kittilä, Pello and central Rovaniemi.
dek: Halo Riverside and Aava Glass Igloos are already open. Arcora opens in Muonio on 14 December, but three other places have not yet confirmed an exact opening date.

body.text: Of this winter’s new places to stay, two glass igloo resorts are already open in Rovaniemi. Four more open during the winter in Muonio, Kittilä, Pello and central Rovaniemi.

body.title: Opening dates as of 19 November 2026
items: Aava Glass Igloos, Rovaniemi: open since 13 November
Kelo Sky Villas, Kittilä: December 2026, date not confirmed
North Resort, Pello: opening date not confirmed
Santa’s Hotel Noelle, Rovaniemi: winter season 2026–27, date not confirmed

body.title: Two of the new igloo resorts are already open
body.text: Halo Riverside and Aava Glass Igloos take guests in Rovaniemi now. Where an opening date is not confirmed, choose a rate you can cancel free of charge.
Rovaniemi: two igloo resorts open, a new hotel in the centre

Halo Riverside is near the Vikaköngäs rapids, about 18 kilometres north of central Rovaniemi. It has 39 glass igloos, and each one has a heated glass roof, a private sauna and an outdoor hot tub. Each igloo measures 23.5 square metres. Restaurant Vuolle by the river serves breakfast and dinner.
The same company’s older resort, Halo Hillside, is about a kilometre from Riverside and has 26 glass igloos.

Aava Glass Igloos is on Olleronvaara hill, about 8 kilometres from central Rovaniemi. It has 13 glass-roofed suites, each with a private sauna and a kitchen, and breakfast is included. According to Euronews, Aava opened on 13 November, and prices start at 499 euros a night.
SkyView Igloo Resort already operates on the same hill, and its rooftop spa and restaurant are also open to people who are not staying there.
body.label: SkyView’s rooftop spa and restaurant

body.text: Santa’s Hotel Noelle, being built on Korkalonkatu in central Rovaniemi, opens during the 2026–27 winter season according to the company, but no date has been announced. According to Euronews, the hotel has 101 rooms and connects to the neighbouring Santa’s Hotel Santa Claus by a covered footbridge.
Muonio and Kittilä: new places on the edge of Pallas-Yllästunturi National Park

Arcora Boutique Hotel & Villas opens its doors on 14 December in Torassieppi, Muonio. It has 59 rooms and villas in total: suites, two-storey sky villas and deluxe villas with their own sauna and outdoor hot tub. The hotel has Restaurant 8, a bakery and a champagne bar.

Kelo Resort in Raattama, Kittilä, reopened after a renovation on 1 November 2025. This winter it adds the Kelo Sky Villas, which the company says open in December 2026. A villa measures 35 square metres, sleeps up to four guests and has its own kitchen. Breakfast is included.
Pello: an all-inclusive resort on Lake Miekojärvi

North Resort is being built on the shore of Lake Miekojärvi in Pello, with 14 villas and two suites. The suites have a fireplace, a hot tub and a sauna. The price includes meals, selected drinks, a private sauna slot, one activity a day, outdoor clothing and transfers from Rovaniemi Airport. The drive from the airport takes about an hour and a quarter.

According to Euronews, the resort opens on 1 December, but the resort’s own website gives no date. Check the date with the resort before you book flights. Stays can be booked through a travel agency or directly with the resort.
Before you book a new place
When an opening date has not been confirmed, choose a rate you can cancel free of charge, and ask the property from which date rooms are definitely available.
New igloo villages will not be built everywhere: the municipality of Inari has decided that large igloo projects will be settled through land-use planning.
body.label: Inari’s decision on igloo building
